readiness: One count: gate(id) in lane O. A deliverable whose records can be counted is counted from them (controls with no requirement: fact controls; connections without a current agreement: lane S's fact connections, else PA.v8bIC; the boundary's SCA review: lane G's v3.G.bnd through its page; SSP placeholders), the rest keep lane G's state. fact('gate', id), fact('nextGate'), the steps table, the card, the panel and the line under the program switcher all read it. Lane G's own counts differed three ways because v2's stage() (3 of 5) and lane G's readyOf (2 of 5) were both drawn.
people lists: Team is the home. Pointed at it: the Overview's Team (reads it), the old People page and its Roles tab (redirected), a gate's who decides, and fact('people') (lane O's override applies Team's assignments and additions, so any page that reads the fact follows). Not pointed, because they read lane F's own constant (PEOPLE_WSX) or v2 markup, not the fact: the ITCSC's section 11 team (12), Authorization's Sharing (7), the SSP's access list (8). They belong to lanes D and E's pages; each needs to read fact('people') and offer Manage → overview-team.

walks.title: From the Overview to what holds PDR back

steps.do: Open WS-X90. Read the Lifecycle section and the card under it.
steps.see: TMRR is open with its five steps listed. Next gate: PDR, due in 7 days, 2 of 5 deliverables ready, three rows with a number each.
steps.was: A strip that linked to a Lifecycle page, which drew the same strip again above a table.

steps.do: Choose EMD on the strip, then Increment 1 in the select, then Increment 2 again.
steps.see: Each phase's steps list under the strip and the address stays #overview. Increment 1 shows its decisions, fielded under the Sep 18, 2026 ATO.
steps.was: A separate Lifecycle page with increment pills and a Steps tab.

steps.do: On the checklist, press Open 4 connections.
steps.see: System's Connections tab on Without an agreement, 4 rows, and a bar at the bottom: Back to PDR · 4 connections without a current agreement.
steps.was: Interconnections opened with no way back but the browser's Back.

steps.see: The Overview, with the checklist exactly as you left it.

steps.do: Press Open the boundary. Request the SCA's review, then Record the review as Accepted. Press Back to PDR.
steps.see: Boundary reads ready with no button. The card, the PDR row and the line under the program switcher all say 3 of 5.
steps.was: Overview said 2 deliverables not ready, the menu 3 of 5 then 2 of 5, the gate showed three not ready.

steps.do: Press Open 14 controls. Click the first control.
steps.see: Controls on No requirement, 14 rows; the control's own page opens with Add requirement as its primary, the return bar still at the bottom.
steps.was: A full-window spreadsheet whose exit led to Controls, a third page.

walks.title: A gate is a page; its decider decides

steps.do: In the TMRR steps, hover PDR and press the eye; then close it and click the row.
steps.see: The eye opens the gate's preview over the Overview. The row opens PDR's own page: deliverables and criteria as tables, a Decision card at the side.
steps.was: A gate page reached from a separate Lifecycle page, with Record decision offered to whoever was signed in.

steps.do: Press Record as Marcus Ryde in the header. Choose Pass, write a rationale, press Record decision.
steps.see: The form says the prototype is acting as Marcus Ryde, and refuses: PDR cannot pass while Requirements, Connections and Boundary are not ready.
steps.was: Approve with conditions went through, recorded by Ingrid Solberg as Marcus Ryde, with no check.

steps.do: Close the form. In Deliverables click the Connections row.
steps.see: The four connections without an agreement, under Back to PDR; the bar returns to the gate's page.
steps.was: A link out of the gate with no way back.

steps.do: In Criteria press Assess on AR.7: Met, and say what meets it. Then Add criterion: choose AR.1.
steps.see: Criteria reads 3 of 4 met with the note in the row, then 3 of 5: AR.1 joins, not assessed. Remove takes it out again.
steps.was: A separate outcome preview; Add security outcomes was a button on the gate page.

steps.do: Open Overview › Team. On Chief engineer press Reassign and choose Ingrid Solberg.
steps.see: The role's row shows her; the Overview's Team shows her as Chief engineer.
steps.was: People & roles was its own menu page; the Overview's Team was a second list.

steps.do: On the Overview choose EMD and click CDR.
steps.see: CDR's page: Decides Ingrid Solberg · Chief engineer, and the header's primary is her own Record decision.
steps.was: The decider was a fixed name on each gate page.

steps.do: Once a gate's deliverables are all ready, record Pass with actions: one action, its owner and due day.
steps.see: The page reads Passed with actions with the action tracked; the toast links to the next gate; on the Overview the strip counts one more.
steps.was: The decision changed the gate page; the Overview and the menu line kept their own counts.

shots.title: The Overview is the program's record

shots.title: The next gate, opened up

shots.title: The records that hold it back, and the way back

shots.title: A gate is a page

checks.walk: v3r/O/walk.mjs on out/v3r2-O.html (the whole build): 119 assertions pass, 0 fail (walk.out): flows 1 to 9 with pages, the three changes on five routes at 1440 and 390, the gate's preview at 390, no page errors
checks.scenes: was from out/prototype-v19.html (V3 on), now from out/v3r2-O.html, same five names

open: The kit's record page keeps two columns at every width (.k3-rec .k3-aside outranks its narrow rule): at 390 the side cards covered the body. Lane O's CSS fixes it for a gate's page only; every other lane's record page needs the kit's fix (asks.json).
Connections are made ready on lane S's pages; the walk still signs the four agreements in data. The 14 controls are mapped through lane C's control pages in the walk, one page each.

Lane G's step-by-step approval chain (ISSM, then SCA, then AO, each recorded apart) is not on the page: Record decision writes the decider's decision and marks the earlier steps 'Recorded with the decision'. 'Reviews first' names come from lane G's constants; only the decider follows Team.
Deliverables and criteria are parsed from lane G's gate page HTML; a change to that markup breaks the rows (the counts fall back to lane G's fact).
Add criterion's picker has outcomes only for PDR and CDR of Increment 2 (v2's own list, read from its dialog); every other gate writes a criterion.
Not passed leaves the step open as lane G does; Request decision afterwards clears it. Checked by hand, not in the walk.
Program settings in More opens the workspace's Settings: no program settings page exists.
Activity shows the 30 newest events v2 draws of 299, with no paging; Export the activity saves the rows shown.
A created program: its gate's page has counts and criteria it can add, but no deliverable rows (lane G publishes none for it); Team assignments made there do not reach lane P's own People page.
The ITCSC's team, Authorization's Sharing and the SSP's access list still keep their own people lists (see 'people lists').
The steps table and the gate's tables at 390 scroll sideways inside their frames; the page itself does not.
Found by the re-walk, not fixed: confirmation messages stay up for about eight seconds and across page changes; the Back to … bar floats over the foot of the page (pages now keep room under it).
Found by the re-walk, not checked at phone width beyond pages opening: tables scroll sideways inside their frames, and the workbook's header controls overlap at 390.

pass2.1 navigation (one sidebar): Nothing of lane O read #rail. Every page of the lane marks Overview in the sidebar, the gate's page included (walked at 1440 and 390).
pass2.2 no vertical tabs: Lane O drew no rail. Its tabs are the kit's horizontal K.tabs (Overview · Team · Activity); Activity's kinds are chips; the walk asserts no side rail on any of its pages.
pass2.3 row to page, eye to preview: A step's row opens gate--<id>; the eye opens the gate's preview, which has Open gate. The next gate's name on the Overview and Details' Next gate are links to the page (they opened the preview). Old gate addresses (lifecycle-<step>, rec--a-work-gate--…, sse, lifecycle-outcomes) open the gate's page instead of the Overview with a panel. The return bar from a gate's page or preview comes back to the gate's page; the panel-reopening state (ov.reopen) is gone. a-people-person on Team and the event previews on Activity stay as they are (v2 kinds with no page).
pass2.the gate's page: Header: what the gate is (sub), More (Export the gate), and the decision as the one primary: Record decision for the holder of the deciding role; for anyone else Request decision, and Record as <holder> (the prototype acting as that person, said in the form). Body: the one next step; Deliverables as a table whose not-ready rows go to exactly the records that hold them back, with the return bar; Criteria as a table with Add criterion (a picker of the NIST SP 800-160 outcomes the gate does not hold, Write a criterion as its first line), Assess and Remove in the row, and what meets each; Actions once decided with actions. Side: Details, and a Decision card (decides, reviews first, requested, recorded by).
pass2.numbers: Checked on the whole build: Operational issues 43 → findings-issues, chip Open, 43 rows (count from fact findingCounts.bySource.issue); Risks without an owner 40 → risks chip No owner, 40 rows; Evidence waiting on review 88 → evidence chip, 1–50 of 88; Your tasks 4 → My work, Assigned to me 4; Requirements 14 → Controls chip No requirement, 14 rows; Connections 4 → system-connections, Without an agreement, 4 rows; Boundary → system-boundary--blk where the SCA review is; Details' baseline (name and count from fact baseline.total) → Controls, All 560; System → system on its default view.
pass2.exports: Export the lifecycle, Export the gate, Export the team and Export the activity are CSV files made by K.save; v2's export dialog is no longer used.
